title: Negotiated Supplier Rate Schedule for Corporate Travel Programmes
content:
Every tier of the Corporate Travel Programmes carries its own negotiated discount on published air fares, published hotel rates and published car rental rates, its own answer on whether the programme reaches the agency's preferred supplier rates, and its own answer on whether travellers may pool their personal club points into a company pool. This schedule publishes all five for the six tiers.

| Programme tier | Negotiated air discount (per cent) | Negotiated hotel discount (per cent) | Negotiated car discount (per cent) | Preferred supplier rates | Club points pooling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Business Starter Programme | 0 | 0 | 0 | Not reached | Not permitted |
| Business Team Programme | 2 | 3 | 3 | Not reached | Not permitted |
| Business Pro Programme | 4 | 5 | 6 | Reached | Not permitted |
| Business Enterprise Programme | 7 | 8 | 9 | Reached | Permitted |
| Business Enterprise Plus Programme | 10 | 11 | 12 | Reached | Permitted |
| Business Global Programme | 14 | 15 | 16 | Reached | Permitted |

The three discount columns are percentages of the published price; preferred supplier rates state whether the programme reaches the agency's preferred supplier rates; the pooling column states whether travellers on the programme may pool their personal club points into a company pool.

## Reading the schedule

- The three discounts of a tier need not be equal. Only the Business Starter Programme shows the same figure in all three columns, and there it is 0 in each; from the Business Team Programme upward the hotel and car figures diverge from the air figure.
- Preferred supplier access and club points pooling begin at different tiers: access is shown from the Business Pro Programme upward, pooling only from the Business Enterprise Programme upward. A programme may therefore reach preferred supplier rates while pooling remains not permitted, as the Business Pro Programme's row shows.
